name: Sidi el Barrak dam
measures: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season)
headline: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season), Water Code protection zone and Dam reservoir or hill lake · 618 ha outside counted PAs · 100% in KBAs

why: In Maden River and Oued El Zouara, KBA with 6 threatened trigger species.
Mostly natural habitat (open water 39%, tree cover 27%, grassland 22% and cropland 6%).
Several measures on the same ground: hunting reserve on a named site (every season), water code protection zone and dam reservoir or hill lake.
The restriction is permanent in law.
Next to a counted protected area: extends and connects it.
Its ecoregion is only 2.4% covered today.

criteria.title: Not a protected area
criteria.text: 88% is already inside counted protected areas (Barrage Sidi El Barrak (Wetland Zone of National Importance); Barrage Sidi El Barrak (Wetland of International Importance (Ramsar Site)); Dj. Chitana / Cap negro (National Park)); only the remaining 618 ha would add to 3.1.

criteria.title: Governed and managed
criteria.text: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season): Hunting banned on the same named forest, wetland or dam in every recent hunting order (art. 12). Water Code protection zone: Water Code art. 123: polluting activities banned in the immediate (10 m) and easement (10-60 m) belts around drinking-water reservoirs. Dam reservoir or hill lake: State-owned reservoir managed for water supply and irrigation; fishing and access are regulated. Legal basis: hunting order saison 2025/2026, art. 12; Code des eaux, art. 123-2; Code des eaux, art. 123-1. Authority to involve: Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF, Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional forest district (CRDA); DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture, dams) and SONEDE (drinking water); CRDA; DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) (Béja governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: 100% of the net area (618 ha) lies in the KBA Maden River (Global/Regional TBD, 609 ha) and the KBA Oued El Zouara (Global/Regional TBD, 8.4 ha). Threatened trigger species of these KBAs: Anodonta lucasi (CR), Serapias stenopetala (CR), Convolvulus durandoi (CR), Calopteryx exul (EN), Pleurodeles nebulosus (VU) and Gomphus lucasii (VU). Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): open water 39%, tree cover 27%, grassland 22% and cropland 6%. Ecoregion: Mediterranean woodlands and forests, 2.4% covered today, under-represented in the protected-area network. It touches a counted protected area (buffer and connectivity). The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Game and waterbird refuge; often state forest under the Forest Code. Drinking-water security; riparian vegetation along the reservoir shore. Water supply; open water for wintering and breeding waterbirds. Supplies drinking water. Sidi el Barrak: built 2000; capacity 275 Mm3; catchment 910 km2; uses: irrigation (main); water supply.

risks: The order is renewed every season, so permanence rests on practice; only hunting is banned; the extent of the named area is approximate.
Narrow belts; the law protects water quality, not biodiversity, so habitat outcomes must be shown; the mapped belt follows the reservoir outline, not the highest-water mark.
Managed for water, not biodiversity: water-level changes and fishing; outcomes must be shown with waterbird data.
Outline from OpenStreetMap: check it against the legal or management boundary.
evidence: Hunting orders over 10+ years, DGF management plan of the forest or dam, waterbird counts.
Decree listing the protected reservoirs, enforcement, vegetation of the belt.
International Waterbird Census counts (AAO/BirdLife Tunisia, DGF), water-level regime, fishing concessions.
next: DGF: confirm the reserve is permanent in practice and map its legal limits; consider a permanent status.
DGBGTH / SONEDE: confirm the list of protected reservoirs and how the belt is managed.
DGBGTH and DGF: compile waterbird counts and agree management of the shores (grazing, disturbance).
authority: Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF, Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional forest district (CRDA)
DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture, dams) and SONEDE (drinking water); CRDA
DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA)
arg.adds: 618 ha outside counted protected areas: +0.004 points of % of Tunisia's land, of which 618 ha in KBAs not covered today.

kbas.name: Archipel de la Galite
kbas.description: The Galite archipelago is situated 40 km off the coast of Tunisia, 45 km north-west of Cap Serrat and 64 km north-east of the town of Tabarka. The archipelago is dominated by the T-shaped main island of Galite (650 ha), which is 5.4 km long and c.950 m wide at the narrowest point and 2.5 km at the widest.
kbas.threats: The site is likely to be declared a National Park. The seas surrounding the archipelago are a Marine Reserve

kbas.description: El Houareb reservoir is a man-made water-body built about 20 years ago on the Oued Merguellil, 35 km east of Kairouan, for flood-control and water-supply purposes. kbas.threats: Uncontrolled hunting is the main threat to waterbirds. There are no obvious threats to the habitat and the site is patrolled by waterworks staff.

kbas.name: Salines de Thyna
kbas.description: The Thyna saltpans, immediately to the south of Sfax, are, with the Monastir saltpans (TN021), the only remaining commercially exploited saltpans in Tunisia, and much the biggest. The succession of shallow pools, of varying depth and salinity, provide prime habitat for waterbirds of all kinds and the constant supervision and wardening means that disturbance is restricted to a minimum.
kbas.threats: The site is a Hunting Reserve. The saltpans are in the immediate suburbs of the large city of Sfax, and so are under permanent threat of urbanization.

kbas.name: Côtes de l'Île de Djerba
kbas.description: The site comprises a coastal lagoon and some islets on the eastern coast of the island of Djerba, in the southern part of the tidal Gulf of Gabès. The vegetation of site is a mixture of sand-loving species such as Ammophila arenaria, Eryngium maritimum and Euphorbia paralias and halophytes including Arthrocnemum, Salicornia and Atriplex species
kbas.threats: The major threat would appear to be from disturbance by tourists who come to visit an historic monument, an old Turkish fortress, within the site. kbas.name: Côte de Zerkine et El Grine
kbas.description: The site is an extensive coastal lagoon with an intertidal area covering 1,600 ha. It is situated on the southern edge of the Gulf of Gabès, 50 km north of the town of Medenine.
kbas.threats: Human disturbance and hunting are the main threats. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Climate change & severe weather Storms & flooding Only in the future

kbas.name: Îles Kneiss
kbas.description: Located 50 km south of the town of Sfax and 25 km south-east of Mahares, Kneiss is a large area of wetland in the Gulf of Gabès. The site includes the surrounding semi-desert grasslands, the shoreline, intertidal flats and five offshore islands.
kbas.threats: The site was declared a Natural Reserve by ministerial order in 1993

kbas.name: Golfe de Boughrara
kbas.description: Boughrara is a large inlet of the sea, between the island of Djerba and the mainland in the southern part of the Gulf of Gabès. It is subject to tidal movement and has extensive tidal mudflats.
kbas.threats: The main threat is disturbance by fishermen. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Climate change & severe weather Habitat shifting & alteration Only in the future

kbas.name: Archipel de la Galite
kbas.description: The Galite archipelago is situated 40 km off the coast of Tunisia, 45 km north-west of Cap Serrat and 64 km north-east of the town of Tabarka. The archipelago is dominated by the T-shaped main island of Galite (650 ha), which is 5.4 km long and c.950 m wide at the narrowest point and 2.5 km at the widest.
kbas.threats: The site is likely to be declared a National Park. The seas surrounding the archipelago are a Marine Reserve

kbas.name: Lagune El Bibane

kbas.threats: Traditional fishing is the main human activity in the lagoon and may be a cause of disturbance to waterbirds. kbas.name: Jbel el Haouaria
kbas.description: Djebel el Haouaria is situated on the northern point of the Cap Bon peninsula in the extreme north-east of the country. The low peak (393 m) of El Haouaria is the northernmost mountain at the end of the Dorsale range.
kbas.threats: The site is protected as a Hunting Reserve and the cave used by the bats has been declared a Natural Reserve. There was a long tradition of bird-catching by local people at El Haouaria; large birds such as raptors were caught for food, using clap-nets on the side of the mountain, while Accipiter nisus were trapped and…

kbas.name: Lagune de Soliman
kbas.description: The site is on the coast at the base of the Cap Bon peninsula, between the town of Soliman and the sea, at the mouth of the Oued el Melah
kbas.threats: The area is situated within 30 km of the capital, and there is much building of housing and industrial facilities. The area has no protected status and some habitat conservation measures are urgently required.

kbas.name: Barrage Mornaguia
kbas.description: Mornaguia reservoir is a recently built reservoir, located 12 km west of Tunis and surrounded by agricultural land. Water is pumped into it from dams in the national water grid, so that water-levels fluctuate considerably and there is little natural vegetation except where a stream flows in; here stands of Phragmites australis, Typha angustifolia, Inula viscosa and Juncus species occur.
kbas.threats: Hunting of waterbirds on the reservoir, although illegal, occurs and is the main threat. kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: Snam
kbas.description: Snam is a small reed-fringed lake, 10 km west of Douz alongside the road to Noueil. It is fed by water which runs off from the nearby oasis.
kbas.threats: The major threats are intensive hunting and the harvesting of reeds. kbas.name: Douz Laâla
kbas.description: Douz Laala is a small thickly vegetated depression, immediately to the south of Snam (site TN041), surrounded by oases and agricultural fields and bounded to the west by fixed sand-dunes. The water is fresh to brackish, and derives from drainage from the surrounding oasis and from winter rainfall, varying in depth, from c.1 m in winter to less than 30 cm in summer.
kbas.threats: The site is privately owned and unprotected. Hunting of waterbirds, particularly ducks, and cutting of reeds are the main threats.

headline: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season), Dam reservoir or hill lake and Water Code protection zone · 48.5 km² outside counted PAs · not in a KBA

why: Mostly natural habitat (open water 59%, cropland 15%, grassland 10%, bare / sparse vegetation 8% and tree cover 5%).
Several measures on the same ground: hunting reserve on a named site (every season), dam reservoir or hill lake and water code protection zone.
The restriction is permanent in law.
Its ecoregion is only 2.4% covered today.

criteria.title: Not a protected area
criteria.text: 100% of the mapped area lies outside the protected areas and OECMs counted in indicator 3.1.

criteria.title: Governed and managed
criteria.text: Hunting reserve on a named site (every season): Hunting banned on the same named forest, wetland or dam in every recent hunting order (art. 12). Dam reservoir or hill lake: State-owned reservoir managed for water supply and irrigation; fishing and access are regulated. Water Code protection zone: Water Code art. 123: polluting activities banned in the immediate (10 m) and easement (10-60 m) belts around drinking-water reservoirs. Legal basis: hunting order saison 2025/2026, art. 12; Code des eaux, art. 123-2; Code des eaux, art. 123-1. Authority to involve: Direction Générale des Forêts (DGF, Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional forest district (CRDA); DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA); DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture, dams) and SONEDE (drinking water); CRDA (Béja governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: Not in a KBA (nearest: Maden River, 18.0 km away). Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): open water 59%, cropland 15%, grassland 10%, bare / sparse vegetation 8% and tree cover 5%. Ecoregion: Mediterranean woodlands and forests, 2.4% covered today, under-represented in the protected-area network. The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Game and waterbird refuge; often state forest under the Forest Code. Water supply; open water for wintering and breeding waterbirds. Drinking-water security; riparian vegetation along the reservoir shore. Supplies drinking water. Sidi Salem: built 1981; dam height 70 m; capacity 555 Mm3; catchment 18,056 km2; uses: irrigation (main); water supply; hydropower; flood control; river Medjerba.

risks: The order is renewed every season, so permanence rests on practice; only hunting is banned; the extent of the named area is approximate.
Managed for water, not biodiversity: water-level changes and fishing; outcomes must be shown with waterbird data.
Narrow belts; the law protects water quality, not biodiversity, so habitat outcomes must be shown; the mapped belt follows the reservoir outline, not the highest-water mark.
evidence: Hunting orders over 10+ years, DGF management plan of the forest or dam, waterbird counts.
International Waterbird Census counts (AAO/BirdLife Tunisia, DGF), water-level regime, fishing concessions.
Decree listing the protected reservoirs, enforcement, vegetation of the belt.
next: DGF: confirm the reserve is permanent in practice and map its legal limits; consider a permanent status.
DGBGTH and DGF: compile waterbird counts and agree management of the shores (grazing, disturbance).
DGBGTH / SONEDE: confirm the list of protected reservoirs and how the belt is managed.

DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA)

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: Steppe de Gafsa
kbas.description: This site includes the area to the north of the town of Gafsa, bounded by Oued el Kebir and Oued Sidi Aich, and comprises large areas of grassland dominated by Stipa tenacissima, with Juniperus phoenicea occurring commonly in the hills. Average annual rainfall is less than 150 mm
kbas.threats: The main threats are poaching of gamebirds and increasing desertification due to the ploughing up of the grasslands for agriculture. name: Abdel Monem dam
headline: Dam reservoir or hill lake · 5.9 ha outside counted PAs · 70% in KBAs

why: In Barrage Mlaâbi, KBA with 2 threatened trigger species; fills 63% of its uncovered part.
The restriction is permanent in law.
Next to a counted protected area: extends and connects it.
Its ecoregion is only 2.4% covered today.

criteria.title: Not a protected area
criteria.text: 92% is already inside counted protected areas (Barrage Mlaabi (Wetland Zone of National Importance); Barrage Mlaabi (Wetland of International Importance (Ramsar Site))); only the remaining 5.9 ha would add to 3.1.

criteria.title: Governed and managed
criteria.text: Dam reservoir or hill lake: State-owned reservoir managed for water supply and irrigation; fishing and access are regulated. Authority to involve: DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) (Nabeul governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: 70% of the net area (4.2 ha) lies in the KBA Barrage Mlaâbi (Global, 4.2 ha). That is 63% of the part of Barrage Mlaâbi that no counted protected area covers today (0.1 km²; the KBA is 92% covered). Threatened trigger species of this KBA: Oxyura leucocephala (EN) and Marmaronetta angustirostris (VU). The KBA outline includes this ground, but its habitat is largely modified: check that the trigger species use it. Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): cropland 86% and grassland 10%. Ecoregion: Mediterranean woodlands and forests, 2.4% covered today, under-represented in the protected-area network. It touches a counted protected area (buffer and connectivity). The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Water supply; open water for wintering and breeding waterbirds. Abdel Monem: built 1964; dam height 18 m; capacity 1.1 Mm3; catchment 25 km2; uses: irrigation (main); river Abdel Monem.

risks: Managed for water, not biodiversity: water-level changes and fishing; outcomes must be shown with waterbird data.
86% is cropland.
evidence: International Waterbird Census counts (AAO/BirdLife Tunisia, DGF), water-level regime, fishing concessions.
next: DGBGTH and DGF: compile waterbird counts and agree management of the shores (grazing, disturbance).
authority: DGBGTH (Ministry of Agriculture) and the regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA)
arg.adds: 5.9 ha outside counted protected areas: +<0.001 points of % of Tunisia's land, of which 4.2 ha in KBAs not covered today.

kbas.name: Barrage Mlaâbi
kbas.description: Mlaâbi reservoir is a small, man-made water-body behind a dam built across a modest watercourse, for irrigation of local agriculture, near the northern tip of Cap Bon, just north of the town of Menzel Temime. Water-levels vary as water is extracted, so there is little permanent vegetation; small areas of Typha angustifolia, Tamarix and Juncus species are found.

criteria.title: Not a protected area

criteria.text: Traditional oasis: Agricultural safeguard zone (Law 83-87): any change of land use needs the Minister of Agriculture's authorisation. Modern date-palm plantation: Regular layout suggests a modern monoculture. Legal basis: Loi n° 83-87 du 11/11/1983 relative à la protection des terres agricoles, art. 5-6 (modifiée par les lois 90-45 et 96-104). Authority to involve: Regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) and oasis water-user groups (GDA); GIAHS team for Gafsa; CRDA (Kébili governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: 7% of the net area (100 ha) lies in the KBA Chott Djerid (Global, 100 ha). Threatened trigger species of this KBA: Marmaronetta angustirostris (VU). The KBA outline includes this ground, but its habitat is largely modified: check that the trigger species use it. Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): tree cover 93%. Ecoregion: Saharan halophytics, 50.8% covered today. It touches a counted protected area (buffer and connectivity). The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Three-storey agro-ecosystem (palms, fruit trees, crops), old date varieties, traditional water sharing; cultural landscape. Date production.

risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.
Monoculture: low biodiversity value.
evidence: Inventory of date varieties and associated species, water management by the GDA, trends in palm-grove extent.
Not a priority.
next: CRDA and the GDAs: document agro-biodiversity and governance; start with the GIAHS oasis of Gafsa.
Keep as context.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: Sebkhet Sidi Mansour
kbas.description: This site is called a sebkhet, or salt-lake, though parts of it have the character of a garaet or freshwater marsh. It is the lowest point of a major plain between Gafsa and Gabès, between the Djebel Orbata and the Djebel Hachichina, where steppe meets desert.
kbas.threats: Overgrazing and hunting of wildfowl are the main threats. Unlike most other flood-plain wetlands in Tunisia, this site has not been affected by dam-building.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

name: Oasis of Telmine
headline: Traditional oasis · 932 ha outside counted PAs · 3% in KBAs

why: In Chott Djerid, KBA with 1 threatened trigger species.
The restriction is permanent in law.
Next to a counted protected area: extends and connects it.

criteria.title: Not a protected area
criteria.text: 100% of the mapped area lies outside the protected areas and OECMs counted in indicator 3.1.

criteria.title: Governed and managed
criteria.text: Traditional oasis: Agricultural safeguard zone (Law 83-87): any change of land use needs the Minister of Agriculture's authorisation. Legal basis: Loi n° 83-87 du 11/11/1983 relative à la protection des terres agricoles, art. 5-6 (modifiée par les lois 90-45 et 96-104). Authority to involve: Regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) and oasis water-user groups (GDA); GIAHS team for Gafsa (Kébili governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: 3% of the net area (28 ha) lies in the KBA Chott Djerid (Global, 28 ha). Threatened trigger species of this KBA: Marmaronetta angustirostris (VU). The KBA outline includes this ground, but its habitat is largely modified: check that the trigger species use it. Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): tree cover 97%. Ecoregion: Saharan halophytics, 50.8% covered today. It touches a counted protected area (buffer and connectivity). The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Three-storey agro-ecosystem (palms, fruit trees, crops), old date varieties, traditional water sharing; cultural landscape.

risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.
evidence: Inventory of date varieties and associated species, water management by the GDA, trends in palm-grove extent.
next: CRDA and the GDAs: document agro-biodiversity and governance; start with the GIAHS oasis of Gafsa.
authority: Regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) and oasis water-user groups (GDA); GIAHS team for Gafsa
arg.adds: 932 ha outside counted protected areas: +0.006 points of % of Tunisia's land, of which 28 ha in KBAs not covered today.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: Ghidma
kbas.description: This semi-permanent wetland is situated 15 km west of Douz, 5 km from Douz Laâla (TN040), and consists of a depression holding brackish water. It is bordered to the east by the Ghidma oasis and by sand-dunes to the west and south.
kbas.threats: The site is privately owned and unprotected. Hunting of waterbirds and sandgrouse Pterocles, the cutting of reeds for making animal shelters and invasion by sand are the main threats.

Traditional oasis: Agricultural safeguard zone (Law 83-87): any change of land use needs the Minister of Agriculture's authorisation. Legal basis: Loi n° 83-87 du 11/11/1983 relative à la protection des terres agricoles, art. 5-6 (modifiée par les lois 90-45 et 96-104). Authority to involve: Local community and the shrine's custodians; Ministry of Religious Affairs; DGF where the trees are forest; Regional agriculture commissariat (CRDA) and oasis water-user groups (GDA); GIAHS team for Gafsa (Gabès governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: Not in a KBA (nearest: Côte de Zerkine et El Grine, 11.3 km away). Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): tree cover 90%. Ecoregion: North Saharan Xeric Steppe and Woodland, 7.9% covered today, under-represented in the protected-area network. The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Spiritual and cultural value; relict trees and old-growth habitat. Three-storey agro-ecosystem (palms, fruit trees, crops), old date varieties, traditional water sharing; cultural landscape.

risks: Low confidence: about 1 patch in 3 looked like a natural grove on imagery, the others were orchards; very small.
A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.
evidence: Imagery or field check of the patch, custodians' rules, community consent.
Inventory of date varieties and associated species, water management by the GDA, trends in palm-grove extent.
next: Check on imagery; if natural, document the customary rules with the community.
CRDA and the GDAs: document agro-biodiversity and governance; start with the GIAHS oasis of Gafsa.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

kbas.name: El Feidja
kbas.description: The site is situated in the extreme north-west of Tunisia, 49 km north-west of Jendouba and 17 km north-west of Ghardimaou. El Feidja National Park represents the best-preserved area of mountainous Mediterranean sclerophyllous forest in the Khroumirie.
kbas.threats: El Feidja was declared a National Park in 1990. Human disturbance and fire are the main threats.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

name: Gulf of Gabès seasonal bottom-trawl closure (0-200 m)
headline: Seasonal trawling closure · 29,883 km² outside counted PAs · 2% in KBAs
kba_names: Côte de Zerkine et El Grine

why: In Salines de Thyna and Côtes de l'Île de Djerba, KBA with 1 threatened trigger species; fills 90% of its uncovered part.
Next to a counted protected area: extends and connects it.
Large: 29,883 km², +29.89 points of the sea indicator.
caps: Temporary measure: fails the long-term criterion.

criteria.title: Not a protected area
criteria.text: 98% of the mapped area lies outside the protected areas and OECMs counted in indicator 3.1.

criteria.text: Seasonal trawling closure: Bottom trawling is banned for part of the year only. Legal basis: GFCM Recommendation GFCM/42/2018/5 (GSA 14), as amended. Authority to involve: DGPA; GFCM (Recommendation 42/2018/5) (Médenine governorate).

criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: 2% of the net area (449.7 km²) lies in the KBA Salines de Thyna (Regional, 287.3 km²), the KBA Côtes de l'Île de Djerba (Regional, 64.9 km²) and the KBA Îles Kneiss (Global, 39.6 km²) and 7 other KBAs. That is 90% of the part of Salines de Thyna that no counted protected area covers today (320.6 km²; the KBA is 5% covered). Threatened trigger species of these KBAs: Marmaronetta angustirostris (VU). It touches a counted protected area (buffer and connectivity). The measure is temporary: it does not meet the long-term criterion.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Lets juvenile shrimp and fish grow during the closure.

risks: A seasonal closure does not give year-round, long-term protection: it rarely meets the OECM criteria on its own.

kbas.name: Salines de Thyna
kbas.description: The Thyna saltpans, immediately to the south of Sfax, are, with the Monastir saltpans (TN021), the only remaining commercially exploited saltpans in Tunisia, and much the biggest. The succession of shallow pools, of varying depth and salinity, provide prime habitat for waterbirds of all kinds and the constant supervision and wardening means that disturbance is restricted to a minimum.
kbas.threats: The site is a Hunting Reserve. The saltpans are in the immediate suburbs of the large city of Sfax, and so are under permanent threat of urbanization.

kbas.name: Côtes de l'Île de Djerba
kbas.description: The site comprises a coastal lagoon and some islets on the eastern coast of the island of Djerba, in the southern part of the tidal Gulf of Gabès. The vegetation of site is a mixture of sand-loving species such as Ammophila arenaria, Eryngium maritimum and Euphorbia paralias and halophytes including Arthrocnemum, Salicornia and Atriplex species
kbas.threats: The major threat would appear to be from disturbance by tourists who come to visit an historic monument, an old Turkish fortress, within the site. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Pollution Domestic & urban waste water Type Unknown/Unrecorded Ongoing Residential & commercial development Tourism &…

kbas.name: Îles Kneiss
kbas.description: Located 50 km south of the town of Sfax and 25 km south-east of Mahares, Kneiss is a large area of wetland in the Gulf of Gabès. The site includes the surrounding semi-desert grasslands, the shoreline, intertidal flats and five offshore islands.
kbas.threats: The site was declared a Natural Reserve by ministerial order in 1993

kbas.name: Côte de Zerkine et El Grine
kbas.description: The site is an extensive coastal lagoon with an intertidal area covering 1,600 ha. It is situated on the southern edge of the Gulf of Gabès, 50 km north of the town of Medenine.
kbas.threats: Human disturbance and hunting are the main threats. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Climate change & severe weather Storms & flooding Only in the future

kbas.name: Golfe de Boughrara
kbas.description: Boughrara is a large inlet of the sea, between the island of Djerba and the mainland in the southern part of the Gulf of Gabès. It is subject to tidal movement and has extensive tidal mudflats.
kbas.threats: The main threat is disturbance by fishermen. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Climate change & severe weather Habitat shifting & alteration Only in the future

kbas.name: Sebkhet Dreiaâ
kbas.description: The site is situated 14 km south-west of Skhira and 30 km north-west of the town of Gabès. It comprises a sebkhet (about 380 ha), an intertidal area (about 200 ha) and the part of Oued Rimth that crosses Sebkhet Dreïaa and ends into the Gulf of Gabès.
kbas.threats: Hunting and human disturbance are the main threats. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Agriculture & aquaculture Livestock farming & ranching Nomadic grazing Ongoing Biological resource use Hunting & collecting terrestrial animals Intentional use (species being assessed is the target) Ongoing Human…

kbas.name: Îles Kerkennah
kbas.description: The Kerkennah islands form an archipelago, 20 km east of the town of Sfax, in the tidal Gulf of Gabès. The archipelago is composed of two main islands, Chergui and Gharbi, and 12 smaller ones.
kbas.threats: The islands threatened by erosion by the sea, particularly if sea-levels rise. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Agriculture & aquaculture Marine & freshwater aquaculture Scale Unknown/Unrecorded Only in the future Biological resource use Hunting & collecting terrestrial animals Intentional use…

kbas.name: Lagune El Bibane
kbas.description: Also known as Bhiret el Bibane (the Sea of Bibane), the site is situated on the south-eastern coast, 10 km north of Ben Guerdane, 20 km south of Zarzis and 15 km from the Libyan border. It is a coastal lagoon 32 km long and up to 10 km wide, with an average depth of 4 m.
kbas.threats: Traditional fishing is the main human activity in the lagoon and may be a cause of disturbance to waterbirds. Threat level 1 Threat level 2 Threat level 3 Timing Biological resource use Fishing & harvesting aquatic resources Unintentional effects: large scale (species being assessed is not the target) [harvest]…

kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

criteria.text: Traditional oasis: Agricultural safeguard zone (Law 83-87): any change of land use needs the Minister of Agriculture's authorisation. criteria.title: Sustained in-situ biodiversity outcomes
criteria.text: Not in a KBA (nearest: Chott Djerid, 1.3 km away). Land cover of the net area (ESA WorldCover 2021): tree cover 90% and shrubland 6%. Ecoregion: Saharan halophytics, 50.8% covered today. It lies 0.3 km from a counted protected area (connectivity). The measure is permanent in law.

criteria.title: Other values
criteria.text: Three-storey agro-ecosystem (palms, fruit trees, crops), old date varieties, traditional water sharing; cultural landscape.

risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.

kbas.name: Chott Djerid
kbas.description: Chott Djerid, situated between the towns of Tozeur and Kebili, is the largest salt depression in North Africa, and gives its name to the whole region. In very wet winters it resembles an inland sea, though water depth never exceeds 1 m; in most years it is a huge area of wet salt, unvegetated because of the high salinity.

risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.

risks: A farmed system: OECM status rests on the agro-biodiversity it keeps and on traditional management; groundwater decline and urban spread are the main threats.
